I've read this I while ago so I may be wrong. My understanding was that the versions you propose are actually indistinguishable. Or that at least we and Oedipa are fundamentally unable to distinguish them. It's an issue of epistemology, and what Pynchon aims at is the contemporary context in which we find ourselves immersed in interconnected information in a way that we can't really say what's real and what's not, we can't differentiate between pattern and noise, since our pattern recognition, search for meaning and hope/belief in higher purpose or order(God, Tristero, conspiracies) tells us there are no coincidences.

In such a social context, seeing the muted trumpet of Tristero in random places becomes a pattern, a symbol, a means of communication. The symbol asserts itself as being a part of an elaborate network, a code in such way that it demands to be understood as a logo of some clandestine operation.

This is paranoia. This is why we are witnessing the explosion of sometimes absurd conspiracy theories such as David Icke. Never before have we had instant access to so much information. Never before could we put any two arbitrary things on the screen together and read them with each other, against each other, or as each others context. And we've never done so much reading and analysis of information. What is happening is that our pattern recognition is pulling out meaning from chaos, and if we can extract it like that from anything, like we extract minerals, then what is left of our concepts of what is real and what exists.

A connection to that is all the business about Maxwell's demon and entropy in the novel, which I've largely forgotten about, but I remember it's in there. We want order and meaning in world, and we are able to find it and impose it on the world, but at the same time we are being told that entropy is inevitable, that it's winning. Chaos and noise will reign. But the ability to discern patterns enables us to have meaning amidst all the chaos. And so the question is what is meaning, truth. essentially, what is the difference between pattern and noise. And even more provocatively: Is there really any substantial difference between "real" patterns and simple pareidolia?

Is there something steering this mess we are in? Is there something opposing entropy of the perceived world? Tristero is at the same time a conspiracy, a conspiracy theory, and a bit of a metaphor for God, the transcendent being, the thing that has the control and in the center of which hopefully lies some sense of truth and meaning. Unfortunately, it's nowhere to be found. It reveals itself only through a patchwork of suspicions, ambiguous clues, rumours and myths etc.

So what emerges from the chaos of the narrative, through interconnection of these motifs and elements, is this question of truth, order, chaos, agency. Your question is therefore exactly what the novel is meant to provoke. Because the process of storytelling and reading bears a striking resemblance to our general engagement with the world through science and mythmaking. How you interpret the world/story/information depends on many factors and it directly influences your understanding of what really happened. The ambiguous nature of the novel is, i think, meant to reflect the general feel of the postmodern times, where a specific new connection between epistemology, narrative myth, information revolution, physical science (principles of entropy), loss of naive religion, paranoia and conspiracy creates a kind of blend where reality and fiction, truth and falsehood become critical questions because they seem to bleed into each other to the point of being indiscernible.

The trick for this book is the Heisenberg uncertainty principle, which the book even glances upon a few times -- the more you analyze this book, the more you aren't sure about what you know.

I have been trying to quit since the beginning of the year after a previous 3-year stint of being smoke-free. Seems any time I make some progress, I fall right back to step one.

10/23/1999, My hubby and I both quit. Our doc prescribed Zyban (aka Wellbutrin) to help with the cravings. We also used both nicotine patches and gum. Granted they're not supposed to be used together, but our doctor said if that's what it takes to quit, as long as we gradually weaned ourselves off both, we would be better off in the long run. Oh, we also consumed about a metric ton of Atomic Fireball candies...

Even with all that, quitting was a horrific bitch. To this day I still get cravings, but hellish or not, it was well worth it.

My previous stint I used the patch for a few weeks, I guess then I was more mentally prepared. This time around the patch isn't cutting it. Tried the gum, can't get past the taste of it, then again cigarettes don't taste much better. Quitting is worth it, every second of it. It felt great to not smoke for that period of time. The list of the advantages of quitting is forever long, while the list of continuing smoking is blank.

I have managed to pull off not smoking for about 3 months twice before. First one was because of a girl I liked a lot, that got me clean off cigarettes and alcohol for a good 3 months. Next one was going to basic training. No choice there for a good 3 months.

This time, I wanted to get a Triumph Scrambler. I figured it would be a nice reward to myself if I can manage to stay smoke free for an X amount of time. So far I'm on day 4.
I started Vaping about three years ago, and within the first week i was down from a pack a day to maybe three smokes a week, I haven't had a cigarette since this past February and it feels awesome.

I hope that makes sense. Whenver I've come across a Postox-hosted image post, I have to actually click the link to the image to view it. I know it sounds lazy on my part, but it's a feature I've grown accustomed to with self-posts, images hosted on Imgur, YouTube videos, etc. I think it'll help Postox catch on more if people can click the little (+) toggle to expand the image from the page they're currently on, without having to open the image in a new tab/window.

I know this isn't something you have access to, and I have no idea if it has to do with the host site being on a "whitelist" somewhere or what, but maybe something you can get set into motion with the admins?

Expandos as they're called are supported if you link directly to the image, like so: http://postox.com/images/2015/06/17/3552694029_de79c201fa_o.jpg

It's not possible for Voat to support non-image links like Postox's image view page automatically (e.g. http://postox.com/image/U for the same image as above). Not just a matter of whitelisting, but specific code has to be added to accommodate Postox (in the same way specific code is needed for YouTube et al).

A feature request for specific Expandos can be made on Voat's Github issue tracker.
